summary: Every row the Dreamer's model-calling adaptors write now records which instruction text produced it. `language_observation`, `room_lexeme`, `exchange_observation` and `room_exchange` gain an `instruction_sha256` column, so a wrong gloss — the one that read `big walk` as a nighttime stroll, for a co-op puzzle video game — can be attributed to a revision, and a later instruction edit can be shown to have fixed it or not.
details: The digest is one SHA-256 over the instruction text the adaptor actually sends (nora/domain/provenance.py). Today that is the inline prompt constant; when the instruction substrate lands it becomes the assembled doctrine plus objective. Same column either way — which is why it ships now rather than with the substrate: a backfill is impossible, so every row written in between would otherwise be permanently unattributable.

The lexeme adaptor's digest covers its extraction instruction plus, when the known-entity check is wired, its verification instruction — that second instruction decides whether a candidate becomes a row at all, so two deployments differing only in `verify_known_entities` write different corpora and must be distinguishable.

`room_lexeme` and `room_exchange` reach no model: they inherit the stamp of the newest observation in each group — the same row `last_seen_at` already reports — so a consolidated row names the instruction currently keeping its gloss alive. The full mixture stays queryable in the evidence tables.

`room_portrait` deliberately gets no stamp: its objective is executed in code with no model call, so no instruction text governed the row. Its provenance resolves through `lexeme_basis`/`exchange_basis`, whose rows now carry stamps.

Migration 0023 adds the column NULLABLE with no server default and no backfill. Rows already in the database were produced by instructions nobody recorded; a default would be a fabricated attribution, and NULL honestly reads as «nobody recorded it». A CHECK constraint on each table refuses anything that is not 64 lowercase hex characters, so a stamp is either a real digest or absent — never a version string that merely looks like provenance.
limitations: Rows written before this migration stay unattributable. That is not fixable — the instructions that produced them were never recorded anywhere.

The stamp covers the instruction text only. Which model ran, which tools were available, and the loop budget are all inputs that can change a row too; the substrate spec leaves those open, and answering them adds a column rather than changing this one.
